label: Usepong
role: To define the symplectic graph of relationships — the knot’s backbone and the complement’s allowed satellite edges.
definition: Usepong is the family of adjacency matrices derived from the knot complement. The mandatory 19‑cycle (x→6→f→…→7→x) is the knot’s meridian — a closed path of type x = x in the HoTT groupoid. The ten satellite strata (cable, binary, mixed, ternary, paired, quadratic, pentameric, hexameric, chiral_pair, hyperbolic_cable) correspond to distinct trefoil companions embedded in the complement. Each stratum is an adjacency matrix whose entries are the probabilities of existence for an additional path constructor. Only these 245 satellite configurations are topologically possible; they form the exhaustive set of 'grammatically correct' extra connections. In the Hamiltonian, these edges become interaction coupling constants J_uv.
manifestation: A Factor binds to one stratum (e.g., 'binary') and a specific satellite_id (e.g., '089'). The mandatory cycle always appears; the optional edges from the probability matrix (e.g., 1↔a with weight 0.3125) are sampled to generate dramatic beats.

global.description: Aggregate of all satellites. Use when the precise stratum is unspecified or for meta‑narratives.

hott_realisation: Each stratum introduces a family of 2‑paths (homotopies) between compositions of the base meridian. The probability matrix is the normalised volume of the space of those 2‑paths.
hamiltonian_realisation: Each edge u→v supplies a term J_uv sin(θ_u - θ_v + chirality) in the Hamiltonian. The mandatory cycle provides the kinetic term; the satellite edges are the interaction potential.
